name: Put a real customer's comment, clip or letter on the screen and answer it
method: Put a real customer's comment, clip or letter on the screen and answer it
do_film: 0 s: the comment bubble, her own clip or her letter fills the picture, untouched. 1-2 s: hard cut to the owner, the product or the hands answering at once. Phone quality, no greeting.
do_words: Quote the real message as headline with the first name, then the answer as the first sentence.
why: It looks like the feed around it and a real person is waiting for a reply, so the viewer waits too.
works_for: Any seller with living comments or letters; cheap and dear, unknown and known; cold; goal: trust, reach, buy.
care: The comment must be real and used with leave; no invented customer.

name: Strike the greeting: begin with a hand already at work or a talk already running
method: Strike the greeting: begin with a hand already at work or a talk already running, so that the first second already shows what the work or the thing is.
do_film: Frame 1: the tool is already cutting this thing, the hand already pouring this thing, or somebody already answers somebody while the thing is in the picture ('Put this in your ear', 'More resistance', 'I'm building ...'). A stranger must be able to say after one second what is being worked on. No name, logo, rules or tour before second 3.
do_words: Delete the first sentence of the draft; ask of each next one whether it catches, teaches, entertains, gives context or proves; begin at the first that does.
why: He lands in something that is already moving and must catch up.
works_for: Creator ads in B2B, beauty and clothing (Denney), making, repairing and renovating trades (Hoyos, Ramos), e-mails and articles (Shleyner), long films (Galloway); in the library beauty tools, shoes, earbuds, kitchen tests, fitness courses. Cold audience, unknown sellers too; goal stop and watch; run-time and conversion winners among them.
care: The running action must be the real job; nothing staged as an accident.

name: Act the trouble and the answer as a tiny skit; one person can play both
method: Act one true trouble and, in the next breath, its answer with your thing in the hand or on the screen: played by yourself as a tiny skit, or dead serious and too far by people who can act; a young firm does not make it its only ad
do_film: Second 0: we are already inside the scene - side A has the trouble or the doubt. Second 1: side B (the same person in other clothes, or a friend) answers calmly, thing in hand. Second 2-3: cut back and forth, one line each. One benefit only. Somewhere the thing lands and something visibly changes.
do_words: Two lines of dialogue as the opening, trouble and answer, like overheard talk.
why: He recognises the talk in his own head and waits for the other side's reply.
works_for: Apps, software, services without a thing to show, bags, shirts, tax advice; phone-shot; cold; goals click and buy.
care: The trouble must be true and the cure must be what the product really does; the shown change is not edited bigger than it is.

name: Say the exact situation only the right one has been in
method: Say the exact situation only the right one has been in
do_film: Second 0: the situation itself is in the picture, seen at the moment it goes wrong, by the sufferer's own eyes if possible (the child slides off the bench, the endless scroll, the police light). Second 0-2, spoken and written: 'If you ...' with one exact detail (two seconds, 100 views, the sentence he says himself) - 'you', never 'I'. Second 3: the turn: 'watch this', or the calm hand that answers.
do_words: One sentence of shared failure, so exact that others read past; for a trade: the trouble, then the usual cure and why he turned it down.
why: He hears his own sentence, so there is no question whether it is for him.
works_for: Dentist, children's goods, software, filters, rehab, teaching; feared or technical things; cold but aware of the trouble; goals book, reply, buy.
care: Name the trouble without frightening; never the fortune-teller's line that fits everyone.

name: A counted list is the promise
method: Promise a true count of concrete things he can use, check or suffer himself (ways, signs, mistakes, stretches, oldest, worst), the first one already in the picture by second 2; a count under ten needs an odd angle or whose list it is; never bare 'reasons', 'tips' or 'elements'.
do_film: 0-1 s: the number and the thing on screen, spoken by the person who does it daily; the first item is already in the picture by second 2. Short scenes, one per item.
do_words: Exact number + 'ways' or 'reasons' + the big benefit. If short (under ten) add whose list it is or what is odd about it.
why: He cannot rest until he has seen whether he knows them all.
works_for: Information, services, clothing with many articles, tours, law, pain relief; known and unknown sellers; goal read, click, buy (Pact's best ad of its year; Good Housekeeping 20 years unbeaten).
care: The count is kept and every item is worth its place.

name: Open on the part of the trouble no rival ever mentions
method: Open with the fear or private thought he really has and the trade never says aloud (found in interviews or reviews, in his words), then the proof of care for exactly that.
do_film: 0-1 s: the thing he is silently afraid for, close, at the moment before it happens (the drawing on the fridge, the crutch by the bed). 1-3 s: his private sentence said quietly by one person, in his words. 3 s: the hand that takes care of exactly that.
do_words: <Side trouble nobody names> is no joke. / Avoid <the feared thing>.
why: Everyone shows the same scene; this one proves the seller really knows.
works_for: Services with risk (moving, surgery, repair, child care), crowded problem categories, new product; cold; goal: call, buy.
care: Found by interviews, not invented; no fear for its own sake.

name: Let him test himself, or his own thing, on the spot
method: Let him test himself, or his own thing, on the spot
do_film: 0-1 s: the question whether his own is bad, as a person says it ('What's a super easy way to know if your mattress is awful?'), large on screen if there is no wild picture. 1-3 s: the test begins with something he has at hand (spoon, egg, phone screen, his own eyes).
do_words: 'Do you recognise the seven early warning signs of ...?' / 'Does yours pass this test?' / a line written in the skill you sell.
why: He has doubted it, could never check, and can now.
works_for: Dear rarely bought goods and troubles people secretly search (breath, bed, eyes, pressure), courses, software for trades; unknown sellers; cold, also people unaware of a trouble; goal click and buy.
care: The test must be true and safe; for a health sign it says when to see a doctor; nobody is made ill by the film.

name: Show the thing that looks like no other in its trade
method: Show the thing that looks like no other in its trade
do_film: 0 s: the one unusual sight of your product or craft, macro, moving: the purple grid pressed, the tool with golden pins, the cut-open marbled clay, the child's drawing beside its jewel. By 0.5-1 s three plain words say what it is. It must be a real property; if it is hidden inside, cut it open or turn it outward before filming.
do_words: 'You've never seen a purple ice cream like this before.'
why: He has no drawer for the picture and looks to find out what it is.
works_for: Unusual colour, shape, tool, material; food, mattress, tinctures, dental, craft; cheap to dear; unknown seller; cold.
care: A real property of the thing, not a colour added for the film.

name: The offer alone, large, for people who know you
method: For people who already know you and on a true day: the concrete offer (price, bundle, struck old price) stands first and largest, next to the product itself or with half a sentence of what it does for the buyer; a picture in the feed that says only 'x% off everything' is not it (as an e-mail subject the percent first did win, o-uzman-072).
do_film: 0 s: product + price or gift in the biggest type the frame holds, true old price beside it, true date under it. No list of claims, no pleading. Before the sale: 'Mark your calendars' and the date, nothing else.
do_words: Offer in the buyer's own world as subject: '10% off comfort you can actually work in'. Start with the offer, then the occasion.
why: He already believes the product; he only needs a reason today.
works_for: Followers, past buyers, carts, true sale days; categories with close prices; local shop; everyday goods. Still pictures rather than film in the sale week (Mei).
care: True old price, true end; no made-up anniversary, no permanent 'today only'.

name: They laughed, then they saw
method: They laughed, then they saw
do_film: 0-1 s: the face or words of the one who laughs or doubts. 1-2 s: the silly-looking start. 2-3 s: a first flash of the triumph (the pavement under the grass), cut away before all is seen.
do_words: They laughed when I … But when I … / She thought I was crazy until …
why: He has been underestimated too and wants to see the laughing stop.
works_for: Skills, courses, cleaning, restoring, new small shops; unknown seller; cold; goal: watch, order.
care: Somebody must really have doubted; one visible triumph.

name: Open in the everyday trouble itself, one only, then the product
method: One visible everyday trouble he already knows, shown in its real place in the first second and ended by the product in the same place; not for fun goods, not for a trouble he must first be taught, no script read at him.
do_film: 0 s: the mess or the struggle in its real place, large. 0-2 s: the complaint in the buyer's words. 2-4 s: the product ends it in the same place.
do_words: Tired of <one exact trouble>? / <Trouble> ruining <place>? then the thing.
why: He recognises his own morning before he knows it is an advertisement.
works_for: Everyday problem products, young brands, small budget; cold; goal: buy. Comedy waits until the plain ads pay.
care: The trouble must be real and common; the product must really end it.

name: Say in one breath what you will do and what may stand at the end
method: Say in one breath what you will do and what may stand at the end
do_film: 0-3 s: first person, one sentence: act, size, the thing that is open ('... until it's big enough to sit in', '... and I have no idea what's in them', '... if I mess this up the whole set is ruined'), while clips already show it. Two facts, not three. No 'let's get started'.
do_words: One sentence: what, how much, what is not known yet.
why: He knows what he is waiting for and that it may fail.
works_for: Challenges, commissions, renovations, craft, food; unknown sellers (potter, carpenter) to the largest; cold; goal watch, follow.
care: The end must come; no stake with money by chance.

name: A big job in an exact short time
method: A big job in an exact short time
do_film: 0 s: the result or the tool, and over it the two numbers: big thing, small time ('30 days of content in 30 minutes', '5-minute makeup routine'). Clock or grid in the picture. Start at once and keep inside the time.
do_words: '[Whole result] in [exact time]'. Odd exact numbers, no age, no sex, no platform named. For teaching: 'N years in M minutes'.
why: People want a bargain on their time, and an exact number sounds tried.
works_for: Routines, courses, software, repairs, kits; cheap to middle price; broad cold public and own followers; click, watch, buy.
care: The time must be measured with a real first-timer.

name: Put his doubt in his own words, then answer
method: Put the commonest real doubt in the customer's own mouth (I / a comment / a person like him), never as 'you think...' reproach and not as a dull FAQ, and let the picture begin the answer within three seconds.
do_film: 0-1 s: the doubt as a person says it - a real comment on screen, an asker's voice, or 'I'd need a plumber for that' - spoken and written. Nobody points at the viewer. 1-3 s: the hands already do the first move of the answer (stopwatch starts, box opens, white mat gets wet). No argument yet.
do_words: The gain and the biggest objection denied in the same line; or "No <time / skill / money>? Then …"; or "How do I know if …".
why: He hears the sentence he was about to say and stays to see whether it can be answered.
works_for: Strange, dear or me-too offers; products one must choose or install; cold and warm; goal: buy, sign up.
care: The doubt must be the commonest one, counted from refusals, comments or calls (Moz asked those who did not buy), and the answer must be seen.

name: Show what is wrong with the thing he uses without thinking
method: Show what is wrong with the thing he uses without thinking
do_film: 0-1 s: the ordinary thing itself, close, in his bathroom, kitchen or garage. 1-3 s: one half-sentence that says what it does wrong, and one picture of it. By second 5: the one decision in making yours that removes it ('different, because').
do_words: <Ordinary thing> should be <what it should be>, not <what it is>. Then: because of this we …
why: He knows the ordinary thing better than any brand, and nobody had told him it was the problem.
works_for: Crowded category, habit products, new kind of product; unknown brand; cold; goal: buy. Not needed for the first of its kind.
care: The fault must be true and shown; no named rival, no health scare.

name: Same odd figure in the first frame of every film
method: Same odd figure in the first frame of every film
do_film: Second 0: the one unmistakable figure is already in the frame, doing something of the day, not lecturing on the product. Same face, same colour, every time. Second 1-3: its small trouble of today.
do_words: The same named figure opens every post and letter.
why: He knows it before he knows what it is about.
works_for: Apps, supermarkets, mattresses, shirts, cups, car dealers; goals be remembered, come back; needs repetition, so not a one-off ad.
care: One figure, owned by the brand; the real product still shown.

name: Cross two things that never meet
method: Cross two things that never meet, where one of them is the product itself, the skill it teaches, or the proof of what it does.
do_film: 0-2 s: one still picture that holds the product (or its skill) and the one thing nobody puts beside it: spreadsheet cells to a dance song, beans on the breakfast biscuit, a man standing on two trucks. Straight face, nobody explains. Test before filming: take the odd thing away; if the claim loses nothing, change the pair.
do_words: Join the two in one short line or one new word ('Build your body with your brain').
why: The mind has no drawer for the pair and stops to make one.
works_for: Dull skills, food, trucks, commodity drinks, golf lessons, dental and health subjects; known and unknown sellers; cold; goal talk, watch, and in several winners sales (Weetabix +15%, Norton's courses).
care: Harmless, clean, and the link to the product visible within the film; Norton's dancing and Liquid Death's crude side are not taken.

name: Ask the small why everybody has half asked
method: Ask the small question about a thing he sees or uses every day, in his own words, never about the seller or his offer, and begin to answer it at once ('Ever wonder why ...? This explains it').
do_film: 0-1 s: the everyday thing itself, close. First words the question everybody could answer and nobody has (why is ..., how long could ..., what does one coin get you ...). 1-3 s: the first step of finding out, done, not told.
do_words: 'Why is it important that ...?' / 'Why does my cat do that?' : a why on a thing he sees daily, with no answer in the line.
why: He has asked it himself and never had the answer.
works_for: Cheap everyday goods, food shops, clothing with a known virtue and an unknown reason, pets, public services; cold; goal watch, and buy (Pact's second best ad of its year).
care: The question must be one people really carry, and be answered.

name: Read out the customer's own odd words
method: Open with one real customer's odd, funny or begging sentence (never a plain FAQ, never an invented one) and within three seconds act it out, read it aloud or do what it asks.
do_film: 0 s: the comment, note or wish itself is in the picture, from a real customer (name hidden). 1-3 s: you do what it asks, act it out, or read the strangest line aloud.
do_words: 'This showed up in our mailbox.'
why: Somebody like him wrote it, and something is done about it.
works_for: Florist, sweets, bakery, crochet kits, jewellery, sponges, orthodontist, gadgets; small sellers; warm and cold; goal watch, trust, buy.
care: Real words, names hidden, leave asked.

name: The buyer's result first, the thing second
method: In a headline, subject line or first sentence for people who have the need: a verb and a visible or countable result first, and the thing named at once in the same line ('Effectively discipline your tween - get the free e-mail series'). Not the benefit alone in a cold ad for a free thing. For film it is not shown.
do_film: Not shown by a film winner; use it as the first plate or spoken line only together with another film opening of the library. 0 s: the result already true in the picture; plate: result and thing in one line ('4 hours back a week: hand me the shoebox').
do_words: Verb + result + the thing: 'Get relief for your weekly migraines', 'at least one more hour of productive time each day'. Turn a resolution ('get organised') into a countable gain per day. Title and noun-phrases become a result.
why: The wish is stronger than any interest in an unknown thing, so he waits for the rest.
works_for: Pages and letters for people with a need, courses, tools, health, home; little-known ingredient or method; goal click, request or buy. Aagaard: for visitors who come by search the benefit line was best, loss second, question last.
care: The result must be one the product really brings; guarantee only if it is given.

name: A real torture test, visible the whole time
method: A real torture test, visible the whole time
do_film: 0 s: the instrument of destruction and the product together in the frame (rifle, propeller, press, blender, blade). One sentence announces the test. Run it once, uncut, the proof never hidden (eggs under glass, not under a seat). At once show it was no trick (break the egg by hand). Test on a phone first: if the gasp is gone on the screen, change the rig.
do_words: 'Will it ...?' or the test with its instrument: 'What happens when you ...?'
why: It could fail in front of him, so he must see how it ends.
works_for: Strength, hold, softness, precision that nobody can feel through a screen; cheap tool to dear truck; unknown brand, small budget (Blendtec: five films for about $50).
care: Really done, uncut, safe; the test harder than the buyer's use but of the same kind.

name: One oddly exact moment instead of the general word
method: Show one exact small moment of a trouble that very many share (the two seconds on the potty, the snagged stocking), seen from his own eyes; the moment is exact, the group stays wide.
do_film: 0-2 s: the exact small scene (the dodged high-five, the potty after two seconds), from his own eyes, words on screen as he would type them: 'POV: …', 'I hate …'. Nothing general.
do_words: Replace the summary word by what it looks like on a Tuesday; copy it from reviews or comments.
why: It reads like his own thought.
works_for: Embarrassing or everyday troubles, dull household goods too; feeds, pages; cold; goal: click, buy.
care: The moment must come from real customers; music licensed for ads.

name: Name the group in the first words: place, trade or age
method: Put the group's own label (trade, owner of X, parents, age) first, as wide as everyone who could buy; name the town only where everybody who sees it lives there (paid local ad, letter, sign), and follow at once with what is true for that group only.
do_film: Second 0: 'Hey Oklahoma City' / 'If you're over 40' spoken and written, in a place that proves it. Second 1-2: who speaks, in five words. Second 3: the question or the offer. Wide enough that everyone who could buy still nods.
do_words: Begin with the label alone: 'Car owners!', 'As an accountant ...', 'Today we ask those of you in Malaysia'.
why: One's own label turns the head like one's own name.
works_for: Local services, donations, car goods, trade letters, pet food; cold and broad targeting; seller unknown; goals call, book, give, buy.
care: The label must be true of what follows.

name: The button says what he will have
method: The button says what he will have
do_words: Replace the act (sign up, order, submit) by the result, best in his own voice: 'Show me outfits I'll love', 'Get the free book', 'A clean apartment without any stress'. Change headline and button together; above a form begin with 'Get ...' and list what comes; keep the word 'spam' away.
why: One last look and he reads what he gets, not what he must do.
works_for: Clothes finder, e-books, cleaning, gyms, office rental, newsletters; first-time visitors; last step.
care: He really gets it after that click.

name: Say what he takes for granted, then one 'but' that turns it over
method: Say what he takes for granted, then one 'but' that turns it over
do_film: 0-1 s: show the thing he already admires or thinks he knows and say it in one short line. 1-2 s: stop, cut, 'but'. 2-3 s: the second half that kills the first (the famous part is the least of it; it looks like X and is not; it went wrong although it was the strongest). The answer comes later in the film.
do_words: Two short sentences. First: what everybody holds true. Second: 'It is not ... / and yet ... / but it can ...'.
why: After the turn he cannot guess what comes, so he waits for it.
works_for: Shown for tech, science and opinion shorts and history films (cold audience, goal watch), and in the library for estate agency, boots, soap-and-water trades and courses; both seen and unseen results; seller known or unknown. A sale straight from it is shown only by the piano course; Kallaway says B2B works too but invented that example live.
care: The turn must be true and the film must hold the second, better thing; never a 'but' with nothing behind it.

name: Put the biggest moment first, then go back
method: Put the biggest moment first, then go back
do_film: 0-3 s: the peak or the finished thing itself (the trick works, the machine runs, the feeling is at its height, several days already passed in quick cuts). Then 'but first we go back to ...' or 'if yours does not do this ...'. Keep the how and the wobble open.
do_words: First line is the finished fact or the hardest moment; second line goes back to where it began.
why: He has seen that it is worth it and now wants to know how it came to that.
works_for: Films over cheap everyday goods (Dr. Squatch, Native), builds and inventions (Rober), long challenges, pranks; in the library tools, filming tricks, gardens, beauty, drama. Unknown brands too; cold; goal stop, watch, and in Raindrop's films buy.
care: The moment shown must really happen in the film; no better scene than the product gives.

name: Name the thing plainly in the first two seconds
method: Name the kind of thing in plain words on the picture within the first second, over the thing already moving or in use; the words never stand over a still picture or a still speaker.
do_film: 0 s: the thing itself, large, already moving or being used (bed comes down, buggy climbs, a pelvis rocks). By 0.5 s three to five bold words say the kind of thing, not an unknown brand name, e.g. 'DIY WALL BED KIT'. Two lines at most, thing and face left free. If a voice speaks, it says the same by 2 s. No greeting.
do_words: First words: 'This is the X' or '[thing] for [whom]'. Delete the first two lines of the draft and start where the topic first appears. Category word before brand word when nobody knows the name.
why: He reads three words faster than he can understand a scene, and knows at once whether it concerns him.
works_for: Unknown product, new category or anything that needs explaining; unknown seller; cold people, often with the sound off; sale and watching. Winners: heat pump, music box, portable power, dog gravy, physiotherapy, woodstain. Not shown for well-known pleasures (chocolate).
care: The words must be what the film really shows; 'the only', 'number one' only with proof.

name: The dull exact name beats the clever line
method: Where people already look for the thing or already stand on the page (search ad, page headline, menu, button, catalogue title, teaching title): say exactly what it is, for whom and where; no pun, no club name, no slogan. Not for cold feed ads or entertainment.
do_film: Cover, first frame and first sentence say exactly what is inside. Show the film five seconds to a stranger and ask what is sold; if he cannot say, take the plain second line and put it first and large.
do_words: What it is, where, for whom, in the searcher's words; no pun, no club name, no brand promise. Swap headline and subhead when the clear one stands below.
why: Somebody looking for a thing wants to see at once that he is in the right place.
works_for: People already searching or already on the page: paid search, shop, menu, button, book title, teaching film, e-mail. Cold entertainment is not shown.
care: The plain line must still contain the gain or the thing wanted; plain and empty is not this method.

name: Open on one clear movement
method: Open on one clear movement
do_film: 0 s: one thing moves and the rest rests, and the movement shows the product: a strap snaps shut, a torch clicks into its case, a thread of gravy falls, a bed comes down from the wall. It starts in the first frame; small moves end inside one second, a slow pour or fold may last three. No second movement beside it, no black first frame.
why: The eye turns to a movement at its edge before the mind decides.
works_for: Things one can wear, open, fold, pour; testimonial films; talking people; cold feed, paid and organic. Dear considered services are not shown.
care: The movement shows the product, it is not a trick beside it.

name: The change inside the first three seconds
method: The change inside the first three seconds
do_film: 0 s: the starting state in hand or frame. By 1-2 s the change on a gesture: throw of the arm, finger on a switch, snap; hard cut in the same frame, or one move, or a time-lapse. By 3 s the finished state stands there; only then how. An exact short time only if true. Things, rooms, work, clothes - never bodies.
do_words: 'From [state] to [state] in [exact time]'.
why: The eye gets the reward at once and stays for the how.
works_for: Visible change of things, rooms, work, clothes; made to order; gift; also long demonstrations for buyers over 50 with many real cases (Savannah). Not for bodies.
care: Both states are real, same light, same place; no staged before.

name: The maker's hands at work, big and close
method: The maker's hands at work, big and close
do_film: 0 s: the hot, shining or heavy material fills the frame and moves (syrup over marble, butter swirling in a pan of fudge, the pot going into the glaze). By 2 s the hands at work; by 3 s the maker's face or voice with one true small thing. Real sound. Never a still hand or a tray that lies there.
do_words: On the shop front: 'see candy made', the process moved to where people pass.
why: People like to see a thing become; they do not know how it is made.
works_for: Sweets, ice cream, bread, pottery, jewellery, soap; cheap gift or dear piece; unknown local maker; watch, visit, order.
care: Clean shop, real product, the true maker.

name: One exact sentence of one real customer as the headline
method: ONE exact sentence of one real customer that names a common trouble or result, alone and short (or the decisive words marked); never rotating testimonials, general praise or an unmarked wall of text.
do_film: Winners are stills, headlines and cards, not films; as a film: 0 s the quote stands alone in big letters over his own photo or the real place, with first name, at most three lines. 1-2 s a marker pen runs under the two or three words of the result. 3 s the product.
do_words: Quotation marks, at most three lines, first name. Simple past 'I' sentence; or a stranger's review phrase copied word for word.
why: Only exact words let the right person recognise himself, and it does not sound like a seller.
works_for: Any product with real reviews, also shy subjects; trust-poor categories; stills and pages above all; cold; goal: click, buy.
care: Her exact words with leave. Never paraphrase a rival's review as your own customer (one teacher says so: refused). No cure claims.

name: Say your own weak point first
method: Say your own weak point first
do_film: 0-1 s: the flaw in close-up or the plain sentence about it, no music trick. 1-3 s: the true cause, which is also the gain, or what you did about it.
do_words: The awkward fact as headline (We are No. 2; our worst result; you can't … without …), then the reason it speaks for you.
why: A seller who says the bad part is believed about the rest.
works_for: Known drawback, price, small size, warnings; sceptical buyers; services with tracked results; known and unknown; goal: trust, buy.
care: The flaw must be real and the gain must come from it; a fake modest flaw is cheap.

name: One question a customer really asked, answered by the expert's own face
method: One question a customer really asked, answered by the expert's own face
do_film: 0 s: the expert in his real place on the way to work (chair, court, shop), coat with name, and the customer's exact question stands on his chest in a box from the first frame. 0-2 s: he reads or repeats it in her words. 2-3 s: the first half of a straight answer. One question per film, from the person's own account.
do_words: The question itself as title, answered in the first sentence.
why: It is his own question, and a person, not a firm, answers.
works_for: Clinics, lawyers, advisers, beauty, trades; local; shameful or dear matters; cold; goal: visit, call.
care: Real questions, correct answers, no advice for an unseen case, no interest product.

name: Open in the real workroom with the real person who makes or sells it
method: Open in the real workroom with the real person who makes or sells it
do_film: 0 s: the true room with the work already moving (syrup on the table, butter in the pan, parcels being taped), no set, no greeting. 0-2 s: the owner or worker stays at it and says in his own dialect what he is doing this minute. 2-3 s: hands on the product, close.
do_words: Written from the bench: where he stands, what he is doing at this minute.
why: It is plainly not a set, so the person and the goods are believed.
works_for: Makers, food, gifts, shops, garages, remote sellers; unknown, small budget; cold; goal: order, follow.
care: The room must be his; a stock warehouse behind a person who does not work there is a false front.

name: Look exactly like the page you stand on
method: In print, on an article page, in a column or a mailing, set your labelled advertisement in the exact look of the page it stands on and make it worth reading.
do_film: No film shows it yet: use it for print, article pages and mailings. (If a film is tried: one real photo with a plain news line, label kept; untested.)
do_words: Set the piece in the paper's, site's or inbox's own style: report headline, upper and lower case, columns, real photo; keep every word useful; keep the word 'Advertisement'.
why: He enters it as reading matter, before the guard against advertising goes up.
works_for: Newspapers, magazines, article pages, feeds, trade press; everyday and dear goods; books, car parts, air conditioners, trade chemicals; cold audience; goals order and lead.
care: Always labelled as advertising; never pretend to be a real publication; the text must really be worth reading.

name: The last person you would expect says or does it, dead serious
method: One person who plainly does not fit by age, dress or voice (or, for a big budget, by a truly famous face) says or does the line dead serious in a scene everybody knows, and nobody notices; use your own idea, not the much-copied young-slang script.
do_film: Second 0: a scene everybody knows (the manor, the office, a game, a shop). Second 0.5: in it one person who plainly does not fit by age, dress or voice - the seventy-year-old, the toddler, the lord. Second 1-3: she says the line with full poise and nobody around her notices.
do_words: Put the plain selling line in the mouth of the one person nobody expects, named and pictured.
why: Eye and ear do not agree, so he must look again.
works_for: Everyday goods, taboo goods, old quiet places, razors, chocolate, creams; tiny and giant budgets; cold; goals be known and buy.
care: The person is respected, never mocked; a false front before the film (CeraVe's planted rumour) is not taken; no coarse words.

name: Keep only the joke that carries the product
method: Keep only the joke that carries the product
do_film: Second 0-3: the funny thing on the screen is a fact or picture of the product's own use. Check: cover the product - if the joke still works, cut the joke. Write the argument into the funny person's mouth.
do_words: The witty headline must be untrue for any rival; if he would remember the joke and not the thing, throw it away.
why: He laughs at the very thing he is meant to believe.
works_for: Computers, shirts, mattresses, toilet stools, pans, cat litter; known and new; goals remember and buy.
care: The point under the joke must be true.

name: His own name or town in the first words
method: His own name or town in the first words
do_film: To one customer (WhatsApp, e-mail video): second 0 the sender's face, first word his first name, then at once what he bought from you. To a town, as a PAID local film only: second 0 a place there, first words 'Hey <town>', the town's dot on a map pops up at second 0.5-1.5.
do_words: Name at the start of the subject line or 'Dear David'; '[City] Community Drive'; a true fact about his surname.
why: The eye finds its own name among thousands.
works_for: E-mails, letters, WhatsApp films, donations, fines, household goods; people who gave you their name; goals open, give, pay, click.
care: Only data he gave you; spelt right; a true fact.

name: Say it is what the trade would rather keep quiet
method: Say calmly, with the source in the picture, the one thing a trade or institution does not print: a practice, never a named rival, never 'you have been lied to'.
do_film: 0-1 s: the source itself fills the frame (label, price list, receipt), a thumb under one line. The speaker says calmly: 'This is what [the trade] does not print on the front.' 1-3 s: the first find is read from the source. Then the next one; the product is where the search ends.
do_words: 'What [institution] does not tell you' / 'The [trade] hopes you will not see this' / take the market's proud word and say what it really means.
why: He is told what he was not meant to have, by somebody who went to look for him.
works_for: Categories where buyers distrust everybody; consumer know-how, food with origin, SEO and other services, publications; cold; goal read, watch, buy. Seller unknown is enough if he shows his source.
care: Only a trade or practice, never a named rival; the source is shown; the reporter is real (Denney's was AI-made); no scare about health without proof.

name: Ask a stranger in the street and let his face carry it
method: Go to a real, unrehearsed stranger with one short question or one true offer and keep the first reaction on his face; film many, publish only a strong reaction; if he gives advice, his standing is written on the screen.
do_film: 0-1 s: your hand, voice or microphone only; one stranger's face, readable. A plain direct question or a real offer ('What's that strap?', 'I'll give you ... if ...'). 1-3 s: his answer or his doubt, uncut. On covers: the door just opening.
why: Nobody knows what a real person will say.
works_for: Samples and street offers, food openings, phone gadgets, sunglasses, business advice, coaching; any audience; unknown sellers; goal stop and watch; two paid ads among the winners.
care: Real strangers, with leave; nothing staged and passed off as chance.

name: Give the thing a new odd name
method: Give a plain thing a new true name that says in itself what it is good for, how it is made, where it comes from or which day it is for (paparazzi-proof driveway, Pocket CB, Cumberland-spiced ...), and let the first picture show that meaning; never an odd name that has to be explained.
do_film: 0-2 s: the thing in its place, in use; the maker says its new name as the plain end of a sentence: 'This is what a mud-proof hotel door looks like.' The picture shows in the same second what the name means (the mud, the hose, the dry floor). The name on screen in two to four words.
do_words: Name the use or the unseen detail of its making ('Laser Beam Digital Watch', 'this pen burps before it drinks').
why: He does not know the word and it seems to matter.
works_for: Dull tools, house features, gadgets, pens, food; known or unknown seller; goal stop and remember, sales in print.
care: The name must be true to what it does.

name: Filth first, the cure at once, no flyer
method: Filth first, the cure at once, no flyer
do_film: 0 s: the worst job you have, close, on clean ground if possible. Within two seconds the first stroke: the jet, the nozzle, the steam leaves the first clean lane. Then each step as one short cut, real sound; days squeezed into about one minute; end on the clean whole.
do_words: On the advert: a plain before/after photograph; the offer stands in the text underneath. No logo card, no telephone-number flyer.
why: He sees the border between dirty and clean move and wants to see it finished.
works_for: Services whose result is visible (pools, rugs, cars, roofs, carpets, dents); unknown local seller; cold people; watching, messages, orders.
care: A real dirty job; never dirt that was put there. Owner's permission.

name: What he uses today beside yours
method: For a young, small or challenger seller in a crowded everyday category: his present thing and yours on the same spot, same light, three to five true differences. Not as the main opening of a mature, well-known brand.
do_film: 0 s: his present thing on the spot; by 2 s yours on the same spot, same light (swap, two columns, one row of ten against one). Three to five plain differences, each phrase copied from reviews, nothing else in the picture.
do_words: 'Here's why we switched from this to this.' / '10 of these = 1 of this.' / two columns.
why: He can always buy from somebody else, so he wants the comparison made for him.
works_for: New or small brand, crowded category, everyday goods; cold people and the last step before buying; still picture or short film.
care: Every difference measured and true; show the old kind of thing rather than shaming a named firm.

name: Say that the advice everybody gives is wrong, and show why
method: Call one common rule or habit wrong and let the picture show the better way at once; never say how many people get it wrong as the whole point, never argue at length.
do_film: 0-1 s: the common practice being done or read out. 1-2 s: "Don't." / a red F / a hand stops it. 2-3 s: the first proof that the opposite works.
do_words: Forget what you know about X. / Common misconception about X. / Don't tell <people> to <usual advice>. Here's why.
why: He does exactly this, so he must know what is wrong with it.
works_for: Professionals, crowded advice markets, beauty, pets, skills; cold; goal: watch, click, trust.
care: The reverse must be provable on screen; no scare.

name: The founder tells why he had to make it
method: The founder's one true event is the buyer's own trouble, said in one sentence with the thing or prototype in hand; for selling an unknown or dearer product, renewed when it tires.
do_film: 0-2 s: founder, plain place (kitchen, workshop): the event or the failed tries, one sentence. 2-3 s: first prototype, old photo or old footage of the making. The brand name may wait.
do_words: Tired of <thing>? So was I. / My own true event in the first sentence, then what I made.
why: His failed tries are the buyer's own, and nobody invents a product for himself to cheat himself.
works_for: Young or unknown seller, dearer than usual, health-related household goods; any sector; cold; goal: buy.
care: The event must be true; a health story never claims or hints a cure.

name: The boss is the joke
method: The boss is the joke
do_film: Second 0: the real owner at his own place, shop name or label 'Owner, 22 years' in the picture. Second 0-2: he fails at the fiddly job (blindfold, wrong hand), or stands dead serious while the young ones fool about, or reads words that are not his. Second 2-3: beside him stands the one who can do it, or his unmoved face is held.
why: The one with the title is the helpless one, and the name of the shop is in the picture all the time.
works_for: Bakery, deli, hotel, bed and breakfast, car dealer, razors; local; cold; goals visit and be remembered.
care: Really the owner, really his years; family-safe.

name: A real thing in the hand, and why it is there
method: In a letter, parcel or printed page: a real small thing fixed at the top that IS the product or its subject, and the first sentence says why it is there. For film it is untested: use only as an idea, not as proven.
do_film: NOT PROVEN IN FILM. If tried: second 0 the thing between two fingers close to the lens; second 1 the speaker says in one sentence where it comes from; second 2-3 the place on the product where it belongs.
do_words: 'As you can see, I have attached ... Why? Two reasons:' - one to catch your eye, one that ties it to the thing sold.
why: One cannot put a real thing away without knowing what it is for.
works_for: Letters, subscriptions, donations, food samples, machines, trade goods; unknown and known; goals answer and order.
care: A true tie; the thing is his to keep.

name: Stop the first picture a blink before it happens
method: Stop the first picture a blink before it happens
do_film: Frame 1: everything is ready and nothing has happened yet: countdown at 'one', lid half turned, blade at the edge, thumb on the button, door about to give. Hold 1-2 s, nothing else in the picture. Then it happens.
do_words: Break the line at the word before the event ('We turned the key and').
why: He has to stay for one more second to make the scene happen.
works_for: First frames and covers; cleaning, drains, cars, lamps, trees, toys; unknown sellers too; cold; goal stop and watch. A shop sale is shown by the lamp and the cookie ad only as long spend or run.
care: The event must come in the same film within seconds and be real.

name: Deal the sentence out piece by piece, so its end lies behind the next step
method: Deal the sentence out piece by piece where the next piece comes by itself or costs nothing (next sign, sheet, slide, page, the second after the skip button); never as three dots at the end of an e-mail subject line.
do_film: 0-1 s: two or three words alone on the screen, sheet, sign or slide. 1-3 s: the next piece comes by a real move (sheet falls, cut, swipe, road sign). In a skippable film begin a new sentence just before the skip button shows.
do_words: End the first screen, page, envelope or slide inside the sentence, at the word he wants; go on at once on the next. Slide one carries only the sharpest three words.
why: A begun sentence is a debt; he goes on to have it paid.
works_for: Everyday goods dearer than usual (soap), services with a plain offer, letters and envelopes, carousels, roadside signs, charity. Cold and silent viewing; goal stop, next page, sale (soap, shaving cream).
care: The end must be worth the step; no cut that hides nothing.

name: Show a thing where it does not belong
method: Show a thing where it does not belong
do_film: 0-1 s: an everyday place, plain light; one thing in it is wrong (bees in a washing machine, a screw in a hoof, sunglasses in a bush, a tiny office under the stairs, a person wholly in foam). 1-3 s: a hand goes to it, nobody explains yet.
do_words: Name the place and the thing in one plain sentence: 'Bees have been living in this washing machine.'
why: The eye knows the place and stumbles over the one thing in it.
works_for: Trades that find things (bees, hooves, drains), small visible products, dull tools, outdoor shoes; mostly cold audience and unknown sellers; goal stop; sale shown only as 'top ad for two clients' (Sanchez) and long run (NNormal).
care: The wrong thing must be part of the job or the product, and really found or openly placed.

name: Hold one small thing right at the lens and name it
method: Hold one small thing right at the lens and name it
do_film: 0 s: the small thing fills the frame, sharp; the face behind it is a blur. 0-2 s: one plain sentence or a friend's question ('Have you seen these?', 'This was enough for a large load'). 2-3 s: what it is made of or what it did.
why: The eye goes to what is nearest and wants to know what it is.
works_for: Small cheap new products (rings, gum, detergent, pasta, watch), also by an unknown seller without a budget; cold; goal stop and buy (Groove Life) or watch.
care: What is said about it must be provable; rivals are not called frauds.

name: What the great ones do when they need it
method: What the great ones do when they need it
do_film: 0-2 s: the known user or the professional in his own need (dentist at the mirror, chef at his own table). Line: 'When [doctors / three names everybody knows] need ..., here is what they do'. 2-3 s: first move.
do_words: 'When A, B and C need ..., here's what they do ...' Take the sale out of the headline.
why: The choice of those who could have anything is the best advice.
works_for: B2B software with real named clients, health, travel, money advice; warm and cold readers; goal read and buy.
care: The named ones must really be clients or really do it; consent for names.

name: A riddle he solves by looking
method: A riddle he solves by looking
do_film: 0-2 s: one thing or a row of three to seven stands still and readable from frame one, label off or places empty, and one question stands on screen and is spoken: what does it cost, which is mine, what is wrong here, what is it called. The question must be solvable by looking. Two silent seconds for his answer. The answer comes inside the film. No prize for a guess.
do_words: 'What's wrong in this picture?' / a guess with a clue ('rhymes with ...').
why: He has an answer ready before he knows it and stays to see if he is right.
works_for: Food before launch, cosmetics shades, small homes, soap, phones, cameras that film themselves, etiquette and decorating courses; cold and warm; goal comment, watch; readership and sale in print quizzes.
care: The answer must be in the film; no prize drawn by lot, no stake.

name: Use the exact odd number, not the round one
method: Use the exact odd number, not the round one
do_film: 0-1 s: the figure as it was counted, large and spoken (512, 7,800 percent, 97.1). 1-3 s: the thing it counts, in the hand. Test two or three true counts if there are several.
do_words: 17 not 20, 1,226 not 1,000: in the headline, with what was counted.
why: A round number sounds made up; an odd one sounds measured.
works_for: Any vague claim: gifts, building material, training, soap, opportunities; print, titles, still ads; unknown sellers; goal believe, click, order.
care: Counted and kept on file; never an invented decimal.

name: Pay the click in the first seconds and stay on the promise
method: Pay the click in the first seconds and stay on the promise
do_film: 0 s: the very picture or words that were clicked. To second 7: what this is. Then no name, biography or rules; the join is already the story. In the first half nothing that is not in the place and the trouble of the title.
do_words: The first sentence under a headline repeats its promise in other words.
why: He checks in a moment whether he came to the right place.
works_for: Long films, landing pages, ads from a strong cover; every seller; goal stay.
care: The cover promises only what the film has.

name: Show the mistake or wrong guess in your own work
method: Show the mistake or wrong guess in your own work
do_film: 0-1 s: the moment it goes wrong, in the hands. 1-3 s: 'we have never … well, now we have', or the first wrong guess said aloud; then the search for the cause.
do_words: How we ruined <thing>, and what it taught us. / exact sum my mistake cost.
why: Nobody shows this on purpose, so it must be true, and he wants to see whether it is saved.
works_for: Distrusted repair, crafts, dear rare purchases, advisers; local or online; unknown; cold; goal: trust, call, order.
care: A real mistake, never at a customer's cost without telling him.

name: Founder: my name, my firm, what it is, in one breath
method: Founder: my name, my firm, what it is, in one breath
do_film: 0 s: founder already moving or with the thing in hand, real place; name and 'founder' written on screen. 0-2 s: "Hi, I'm <name>, founder of <firm>." 2-3 s: what it is, price or the one thing it does.
do_words: I'm <name>, <title> of <firm>, and I make <thing> for <people>.
why: A named person who puts his face to it feels less like an advertisement.
works_for: Cheap everyday goods, inventions, local services; unknown seller; cold; goal: buy. Denney: US audience above all; other countries not shown by her.
care: He must be the real founder; the offer must be said at once, not a life story.

name: Do you make these mistakes with …?
method: Promise to show the (few, counted or "these") mistakes that even careful people make with a thing in which he cannot judge himself and fears the expert; never in matters of taste, and without scolding him.
do_film: Proof is print, mail and headlines; film not shown. 0-1 s: one of the mistakes being made by a hand, close, unnamed. 1-3 s: "These mistakes even careful <people> make with <thing>"; a number on screen counts 1 and the first one is stopped.
do_words: Keep the skeleton, change the noun: Do You Make These Mistakes in/with <X>? The body gives the actual mistakes.
why: He uses the thing every day and cannot be sure he is right.
works_for: Any product whose users make visible mistakes without it; language, vitamins, meetings, rooms, trades; cold.
care: The mistakes must be real and given in the piece.

name: Half a small private story in the headline, then stop
method: Half a small private story in the headline, then stop
do_film: Proof is headlines, letters and print. 0-1 s: the awkward second itself, frozen just before the turn (the laughing faces, the hand on the piano lid). Text or voice: the one half sentence with its "so I …" or "but when I …". 3 s: still no end; the film tells it fully.
do_words: My <person> <did awkward thing>, so I … / She could hear every word, so she …
why: He may have the same at home and wants to know how it ended.
works_for: Everyday product with a private annoyance, skills, causes; unknown; cold; goal: click.
care: The story must be true and must be finished in the piece.

name: Rename the thing so that the name alone says what he gets
method: Rename the thing so that the name alone says what he gets
do_film: First words on screen, sign or menu are the name: taste, place or use in it (Cuban Black Bean Soup; The Queen of Christmas Presents).
do_words: Take the virtue or category word out, put taste, place, use or occasion in: 'Cumberland-Spiced Veggie Sausage & Mash' for 'Meat-Free Sausage and Mash'.
why: He judges by the name, long before he knows the thing.
works_for: Menus, shop cards, books, gifts, small services with little advertising money; everyday and cheap goods.
care: The name must be true and free to use.

name: First picture: the broken thing; then find the cause
method: First picture: the broken thing; then find the cause
do_film: 0 s: the sick part fills the frame, camera creeping in, complaint in one calm sentence ('this one was limping'). 1-3 s: the culprit is already half seen. Then hands take it apart.
do_words: The complaint, then 'and as soon as I opened it I found out why'.
why: He sees that something is wrong before he is told what, and waits for it to come out.
works_for: Repair, cleaning, animals, dental, inspection; work outsiders never see; unknown; cold; goal: watch, trust, send in.
care: A real case, consent, no disgust for its own sake.

name: Do it for one named person, for a true reason
method: Do it for one named person, for a true reason
do_film: 0-2 s: who it is for and why, in one sentence, while the hands already work. 2-3 s: one flash of the end (handing over), cut before the face reacts.
do_words: Making <thing> for <person> because <true reason>.
why: A reason makes him care, and he waits to see that person's face.
works_for: Handmade, repair, local service, small stakes; unknown; cold; goal: watch, follow, order.
care: Person, reason and consent must be real; no staged pity.

name: One true private event, told by the one who lived it
method: One true private event, told by the one who lived it
do_film: 0 s: the one who lived it, alone, where it happened or across a table, already speaking; no music, no logo. 0-3 s: the event itself as first sentence, exact (day, sum, place), then one second of silence. If he is unknown, the thing that proves it lies in the frame.
do_words: I have <event>. / The exact mistake and the exact sum, first line.
why: A true event cannot be skipped the way a script can.
works_for: Creators living the situation, advisers, family goods, things of taste; cold; goal: trust, buy.
care: Must have happened to that person; no borrowed grief.

name: Put the oldest of the house before the camera
method: Put the oldest of the house before the camera
do_film: Second 0: the old hands or face, at work or nose to nose with the thing, very close. Second 1-3: one gesture or one dry word of the old one; the younger stays at the edge.
why: Age and work in one face are believed before a word is said.
works_for: Cake shop, guest house, deli, candy maker, farm, tools, supermarket; small and local; cold; goals watch and visit.
care: She wants to; really of the house; dignified.

name: Staff play a small comedy of their own workplace, already under way
method: Staff play a small comedy of their own workplace, already under way
do_film: Second 0: somebody walks into the scene and says the first odd thing ('We just got a new hire and we wanted you to train him'), name of the shop in the picture. Second 2-3: cut to the face that must bear it. A real small event of the week is the plot; the same day every week.
do_words: One line on screen tells the mishap: 'when a customer drives off with our iPad'.
why: Everyone has sat in that room: 'that could be at my work'.
works_for: Car dealer, hotel, software, coffee stand, tea, food van; staff who like it; cold and local; goals be known, be remembered, hire.
care: Staff take part willingly; nobody is shamed; clean humour; own real workplace.

name: Play the absurd dead seriously
method: For being seen and talked about (and for selling only when the name is already loved): play one thing of your own trade, the product in the picture from the first second, in a grave form done with real craft, nobody smiling; never as the first ad of a young seller, never in a reminder from an office or a clinic.
do_film: 0-2 s: the product or the trade itself in frame one, in the dress of something grave: an operation, a documentary close-up, an official warning, a battle speech, a candle-lit dinner. One subject, slow, nobody smiles, real light and sound. Example: steel table, gloved hands, a syringe already in a toy: 'Can you transplant goo from one squishy to another?' The real tool or service wins at the end.
why: The form says serious, the subject says not; the eye waits for the crack.
works_for: Loved brands with nothing new to say, toys, sandwiches, trees, plates for weights; better with a known name or good craft; goal talk and watch.
care: Good craft; nobody's grief or faith is the joke.

name: Open with something useful that is free, sell a step later
method: When the first aim is a name, a request or a first taste (not a sale today): open with one named free thing shown or said whole (guide, list, catalogue, food sample, first wash) together with what it does; not for health and beauty goods.
do_film: 0 s: the free thing itself in a hand, big, its cover or portion readable (list, guide, catalogue, a spoonful of the food). 1 s: one sentence: what it is, how much of it, which trouble or pleasure it brings. 2.5 s: how to get it (one word, postage, at the door). The paid product is not shown yet.
do_words: 'Get the free ...' names the thing; subject line gives a real nugget before anything is sold.
why: The first step costs nothing, so no resistance wakes.
works_for: Cold strangers; dear or considered purchase; services; cheap product of unseen quality (tester for postage); expert's own account.
care: The gift must be worth having by itself; no hidden subscription.

name: A short private letter from one named person
method: A short letter or e-mail from one real named person to people who already know him, his post or his house (customers, members, staff, people who asked); if the name is unknown, the house stands beside it in the sender line.
do_film: Still for a feed: 0 s: a phone or paper page filling the frame: From: <real name, house>; Subject: <short, as to a colleague>; "Dear …" and the first sentence in readable size, a hand-written name below. For a film: 0-3 s: that person alone, sitting, one lens, says only the first sentence of his letter. Nothing that sells in the frame.
do_words: Sender = a person; subject like a colleague's ('Quick question'); first line to him alone.
why: It feels meant for him and not for the crowd.
works_for: Launches, sales, dear offers, causes, advisers; own customers above all; goal: open, buy, give.
care: The sender must be real and have written or read it; no invented customer as sender.

name: Home-made phone film instead of the polished one
method: For an everyday thing or service shown to people who do not know you, film it plainly by phone in the place where it is used, and run it beside the polished one; a brand that lives on a premium look keeps its polished film.
do_film: Second 0: the phone, held in the hand, is already where the thing is used (kitchen table, garden, van); no logo, no studio light. Second 1: the thing comes in from the camera's side or is already in use. Second 2-3: one plain sentence as to your mother. Make the same message twice, polished and plain, and run both.
do_words: A snapshot of the real thing on the workbench instead of the brochure, with one plain line.
why: It looks like what friends post, so it is watched before it is judged as advertising.
works_for: Everyday and household goods, food, beauty, set-up services; small and large sellers; cold feeds; goals buy and book. For a brand that lives on a premium look the polished film has its place (Fogarty).
care: It must be the real place and the real hand; the picture stays sharp and lit enough to see the thing; plain is not careless.

name: Hold the brand back until his trouble or the story stands
method: In a film he may skip, hold name and pack back while one true story or one trouble stands (at most about second 15 to 37), when the aim is being watched, passed on or believed; not for a cheap thing understood at once, not where the name must be learnt (then a small mark in the corner).
do_film: 0-3 s: one person and one trouble or one small true event, already under way; no name, no pack, no mark, no seller's word. Next 10-30 s: the same event goes on and gets worse or closer. Then the thing enters as its answer, shown in use, and only then the name.
do_words: First paragraph without your name; the product enters as the answer.
why: Nobody cares about a brand yet, but everybody cares about his own trouble or a true story.
works_for: Cold audience, problem products, founder with a true event, known shop in season. Not for a cheap thing understood at once (Dubin gives price and product in the first breath).
care: The end must really answer the beginning; otherwise it is a trick.

name: Something everybody knows, with one thing changed
method: Something everybody knows, with one thing changed
do_film: Second 0: a form everybody knows at a glance and exactly right in every detail (a car commercial at sunset, the witch's house, the carrot on Christmas night). Second 1-2: exactly one thing is wrong, and it is yours (the driver turns and says it is an ad for washing powder; a shake instead of the children). Second 3: the first sentence says the change. Nothing else is changed.
why: It is understood at once and yet not seen before.
works_for: Series, odd or new products, cold audience.

name: Say or show the harmless thing the others are afraid to
method: One plain picture and one flat, harmless sentence against a habit everybody has an opinion on, with a straight face, said by a maker or brand whose standing people know or can see; never on suffering, faith, politics or a rival's person; tried first on the own page.
do_film: 0-2 s: one plain picture or one flat sentence everybody will have an opinion on; nothing to understand, only to object to; straight face. Choose, of two openings, the one that makes you nervous. Look for the sentence that begins 'I was hoping we wouldn't have to go there'.
do_words: The sensitive true fact as the headline, not the features.
why: People stop to object, and a seller who dares is believed.
works_for: Known cheap food, learning app, herbal drinks with real origin, airline, car, a client's product when features did not bite; mostly known brands or a maker with standing; goal talk, then buy (Weetabix +15%).
care: Nobody is put down, no sacred or political thing, true to the last word; on a page that can be taken down.

name: Say it in the buyer's word, not the trade's
method: Say it in the buyer's word, not the trade's
do_film: Take the first spoken sentence; replace every trade word by the word buyers type, say or write in reviews. Put that word on the plate at 0 s and show the thing under it.
do_words: Collect one blank sentence from visitors ('I want a wallet that ____'), reviews, search counts; take the phrase of the biggest pile as headline. Replace local names by words the whole world knows. A series gets the name its viewers already use.
why: He recognises his own thought and need not translate.
works_for: New or technical products, expert services, crowded shops, global accounts; cold people and people who are searching. Cheap and dear.
care: Words must be copied from real buyers, not invented by the seller.

name: Cut the frame into two opposed halves
method: Split the first frame only when the two halves are the same person, place or thing in two states that can be told apart at a glance (beginner/advanced, before/after, old/new), or the silent product beside the person who speaks. Never two talking halves, never as decoration, not for pure memory campaigns on TikTok.
do_film: Frame 0 is split: left/right or top/bottom, and the halves differ in colour and state (dead/green, tired/awake, talking/silent proof, beginner/advanced). The same person or place in both. Something moves in one half.
why: In a full-screen feed a split picture makes him look twice, and his eye compares by itself.
works_for: Visible difference of any kind: gym, mattress, land, exercise, photography levels; cold feed; Dara uses it to go down a list of failed tries without naming a rival.
care: Both halves real; no body before/after in paid ads.

name: An absurd scene that could belong to no other product
method: With professional writers and players and money to film it: one pleasant, striking, dream-like enlargement of the product's own truth in the first five seconds, then the product on screen. Not outrageous or disgusting, not a joke by amateurs, not as the first film of a young brand without proof.
do_film: 0-3 s: one striking, pleasant, dream-like picture of the product's own truth enlarged: a closed eye opens and a woman falls through the sky towards a bed; commentators at a giant desk watch a man work. Test: surprising AND could it stand for another product? By 5 s the product is in the picture.
why: He has not seen it, and it still makes sense.
works_for: Mostly large production: furniture, chocolate, software, bathroom products; skippable video; unknown brands too (Squatty Potty).
care: No toilet jokes or bare skin needed; take the form.

name: A small honest condition, then the strong promise
method: A small honest condition, then the strong promise
do_film: 0 s: the small cost in the picture (a minute on a clock, one sheet, one tool). Sentence: 'If you've got N minutes ...' or 'Give me N minutes'. Same sentence: what he gets. Next lines: why so little is enough.
do_words: 'If you've got 20 minutes a month, ...'; 'Spend a minute. Save an hour.'
why: The condition makes the promise believable, and he has already half agreed.
works_for: Promises nobody believes any more: courses, newsletters, health habits, planners; cold mail, explaining film.
care: The promise must be provable with exactly that condition.

name: Point at the exact spot
method: Point at the exact spot
do_film: 0 s: the thing or the fault large in the picture. Before 0.5 s an arrow, a finger or the mouse lands on the exact spot and stays; with it one to four words: what it is called or what to do ('Fix This', 'DON'T DO THIS', the exact name of the result). 1-2 s: the hand starts on that very spot. A speaker, if any, stands small below and points up.
do_words: On a cover: remove the clutter, leave one thing large and a cursor on it.
why: He looks where a finger points, and one spot is understood at once.
works_for: How-to, body posture, grooming, software, odd objects, other people's inventions shown by a talking head.
care: No health fright; the spot must be what the film explains.

name: The one who doubted it is the one who tells
method: The one who doubted it is the one who tells
do_film: 0-2 s: text or voice: the doubt in past tense ("I thought this was a scam", "my teenagers are too cool for everything"). Cut before the reason. 3 s: the moment that turned it, in the picture.
do_words: I thought <doubt>. / <The hardest person to please> <did the surprising thing>.
why: The past tense says the doubt broke, and he must know what broke it.
works_for: Unknown online seller, dear fun goods, food for children, crowded categories; cold; goal: buy.
care: The doubter and the turn must be real.

name: Say the first line in your own calm voice
method: When the picture itself is strong (hands at work, a find, a big act), say the first line as to a friend: low, natural, tight, no greeting, no shouting. Not for live selling and not for a talking head without anything to see.
do_film: 0 s: close on the thing in the hands or the find, nothing else in the frame; the camera creeps nearer. 0-2 s: one tight sentence in the everyday voice, recorded close, that says what is wrong or what he found. No greeting, no music on top, every pause cut. 2-3 s: the first move of the hand.
why: A natural voice does not announce an advertisement, and the picture holds him.
works_for: Hosts, owners, trades on camera; feeds; cold; goal: watch, trust.
care: His own voice; calm is not sleepy.

name: Turn the unseen effect into one object everybody knows
method: Turn the unseen effect into one object everybody knows
do_film: 0-1 s: the stand-in object alone, doing what the product does inside the body or the machine (butter melting, a hose with a kink, a tomato under the brush, ten bags beside one). 1-3 s: the product stands beside it and one short line joins the two.
do_words: Turn the figure into something he can picture: '5 miles of walking', 'Uber Eats for the sun'.
why: He understands at a glance what he could not see.
works_for: Unseen results: slimming, gut, gums, vitamins, detergent power, steering, technical news; cheap and dear; unknown sellers too; cold; goal understand and buy.
care: The comparison must be true in size; a health effect needs proof; no toilet joke.

name: Name the gain exactly and cover the how
method: Say the exact gain so plainly that it could stand as the title, and cover only the one move that brings it; never a vague 'trick' or 'secret' without the gain.
do_film: 0 s: the gain itself as a picture that can be checked (a bottle that cannot be pulled through the lock, a dress without a crease). 0-2 s: one sentence with the exact gain and the place. 2-3 s: the hand starts the move and the body or a cut covers it. The move is shown whole in the last third. (No film in the library proves this; words do.)
do_words: Read the product, mark a useful surprising instruction, write the gain and the place and hide the move: 'How to make your car very, very hard to steal' (page number behind it). On an envelope or thumbnail set: the four that touch four different everyday wishes.
why: He knows what he will get and cannot guess how.
works_for: Information, courses, guides, services with know-how, products people will ask about, case stories; mixed audiences; unknown sellers; goal open, read, watch to the end.
care: Twist, never distort: the answer stands there and is 100% true.

name: The finished thing first, then how or what it was
method: The finished thing first, then how or what it was
do_film: 0 s: the complete, finished effect running or standing there (the trick in a loop, the ordered cupboard, the curl of wood, the green ground). Maker's hand or eye at the edge. 2-3 s: hard cut to the raw state, or 'here is how'.
do_words: Title names the finished wonder, the next line says it is done with ordinary means.
why: He sees that it is possible, and wants the way back to the beginning.
works_for: Skills people think need an expert, order in the home, land, craft tools; services without an object: the result with the offer on it. Goal watch, save, buy.
care: Follow at once with the true raw state.

name: An impossible-looking act, really done, no visible cut
method: Within the first two seconds a real thing does what the eye does not expect of it (a coin floats on metal, a row of books lifts as one piece, a wall becomes a bed, a cane stands alone), in one shot without a visible cut, really done; the true means is seen soon after.
do_film: 0 s: a normal-looking thing, close, one steady shot. Within 2 s it does what it should not: the wall tips down and is a bed, the coin floats, the cane stays standing. No cut until it is done. Then let the true means be seen. Nothing generated, nothing speeded.
why: He watches it again to find out how.
works_for: Fragrance, cars, skill teachers, toys, reflective or moving products; known brands mostly, trick makers also; watching and sharing.
care: Really filmed; a generated picture must not carry a product claim. Speaker dressed.

name: Put the hidden reason people really buy first
method: Find in your best film, reviews or best buyers the one reason they really give for buying, and put that first in plain words, before the merits of the thing; do not guess a dream.
do_film: Take the best film or the best customers; find the detail that really sells (looking good, saving tax, being ready in five minutes). 0 s shows only that, on a person in use. Merits (titanium, formula) come later.
do_words: Headline = the wish, though the product does not carry the word ('The Ultimate Tax Shelter'); or what owning it says about him ('You don't need accessories, you need gear').
why: He buys what it does for him, not what it is.
works_for: Things others see on you, dear everyday objects, books and services with a consequence; accounts that already have a winner to study.
care: The body must show truthfully how the product leads to the wish.

name: Build or find the one sight people travel for, and show it first
method: Build or find the one sight people travel for, and show it first
do_film: 0 s: the one sight, framed as a visitor would take it, already happening: the cow's tongue reaching the bread, the bucket filling, the swimmer behind the window, the guide playing in the light. One take, the camera walks in or stands still; a visitor's hand or back may be in it. No sign, no tour, no speech in the first three seconds. Where it is and when: after 4 s.
why: He sees himself standing there with his own phone.
works_for: Places: stays, farms, cafés, parks, shops; local or two hours away; visits and direct bookings.
care: The sight must be there every day for every visitor; animals treated well.

name: Leave the hated old way behind in one line
method: For a young or unknown seller whose product replaces a known chore or disliked form: one line leaves the old thing behind while its successor is already seen at work within three seconds; name the old KIND, not a firm.
do_film: 0 s: the old thing or old chore (the pile of tools, the glue, the heater) with a line over it: NEVER … AGAIN, or a note on it: 'I don't need this because …'. 1-3 s: one move of the new way.
do_words: Never <old chore> again. / You don't have to settle for <old way> that <its exact trouble>.
why: He hates the old way already; the line gives him leave to drop it.
works_for: Products that replace a chore or a disliked form; household, craft, dental, pets; unknown seller; cold; goal: buy.
care: The old way must really be gone.

name: Make the thing they tease you for your own joke
method: Take one thing customers REALLY tease or rate you down for (their clip, their one-star line), show it untouched first and own it in one dry line tied to your price or product; only where the value is sure.
do_film: 0-2 s: the complaint as customers say it, their clip or their line. 2-3 s: hard cut to the brand, its figure or its product, one dry line that owns it and is tied to the price or the product.
do_words: Print the one-star review, or 'what you expect for <low price>'; or admit in huge letters that this is an advertisement.
why: He expected a defence and got a joke at the seller's own expense.
works_for: A brand with a known quirk or weak point, or a cheap new brand; social feeds; goal: reach, being liked, sales where the value is sure.
care: Review must be real; no swearing, no laughing at the customer.

name: An unlikely person did it
method: The person from whom nobody expects it does the very thing that is sold, and his unlikeliness touches exactly that skill; the result is seen or provable, the how stays open.
do_film: 0 s: the unlikely person plainly seen (age, body, place) with the tool of the skill in his hand, others watching. 1-3 s: he begins to do it and it works: first stroke, first word read, first note; a face beside him changes. One line: who he is and what he does. No explanation.
do_words: How a <plain, unlikely person> <startling result>. / I am not a doctor …
why: If such a person can do it, so can he, and the experts may be wrong.
works_for: Markets where buyers were disappointed by experts; skills, sport, courses, home products; unknown seller; cold.
care: The person and the result must be real; drop Halbert's health claims.

name: Call those who already want it
method: In the first words name the wish itself to the person who already has it ('If you've wanted to ...', 'Would you like to ...', 'To X who would like Y'), the wish seen fulfilled in the picture. Where the reader can test himself on the spot, try a quiz first: it beat this shape.
do_film: Second 0: the wish already fulfilled fills half the picture (green raised bed, the sprayed car door), the speaker in it, hands at work. Second 0-2, into the lens: 'Would you like to <the wish, in his words>?' or 'If you've wanted to ...'. Second 3: the one thing that stood in his way (price of the tool, no room).
do_words: 'To men and women who want ...' or 'If you've ever wanted to ..., this is for you. Here is why:' - then a true story. No warm-up, no statistic proving that the problem exists.
why: A wish that burns already only needs to be fed.
works_for: Courses, paint guns, writing aids, magazines; mixed crowds; unknown seller; goals read on, order.
care: Promise only what the thing gives; no income promises.

name: The topic of the day, only if it acts out your product's own truth
method: On a daily account whose goal is to be seen and followed: take the topic of the day only the same day and only if your thing does its one true job inside it in one plain line; otherwise let it pass. Not a plan for bringing customers.
do_film: The same day. Second 0: the thing everybody talks about is seen at once (two flags, the named storm, the pie behind bars). Second 1-2: your thing at its ordinary work inside it (two confectioners snapping candy for two teams). Second 3: one line in which it would have helped, or the rival's own phrase turned. Nothing ready within the hour: no film.
do_words: One line under the news: the product would have helped, or the rival's own phrase turned.
why: The news has told the story already; only the last line is missing.
works_for: Airline, language app, chocolate, supermarket, soap, candy; daily accounts; known and small sellers; goals be seen and remembered.
care: No grief, race or religion; no other firm's characters without right.

name: Open a second question right after the first
method: Open a second question right after the first
do_film: 0-3 s: the first hook. Then, before the first answer is finished, one line that promises a concrete second thing ('and that is not even the strangest part: wait for the drawer'), and again between value two and three. In a long film the second question stands by second 30 and a side story before the half.
do_words: First sentence makes one point; second sentence names one more, still unseen, by a word the reader can picture ('... and the second photograph is worse').
why: A question that is still open keeps him; when one closes, the next already stands.
works_for: Teaching reels, tech shorts, long films; the people speak of watching to the end, not of selling; cold audience; every size of seller. In the library it also stands in repair, cleaning and phone-test films.
care: The second thing must be named by something concrete and must really come.

name: Show the true reaction first, its cause later
method: Show the true reaction first, its cause later
do_film: 0-2 s: one face, close, at the first bite, look or touch; real and unrehearsed; the thing is outside the frame. One or two cuts later the cause. Brief the person to try it for the first time with the camera running.
do_words: First person, the feeling first and the thing unnamed: 'I knew which one, and it still ...'.
why: Another person's strong feeling is a question until he knows what it is about.
works_for: Things with an immediate effect: food, beauty, sunglasses, toys, pans, tested gadgets; emotional products; cold; goal stop, and sale in BluBlocker and Javvy.
care: First time must be the first time; no paid amazement.

name: Speak to him on the day it happened
method: Speak to him on the day it happened
do_film: 0-1 s: the event of his day stands in the picture (the new car in the yard, the flashing lamp, the keys) or the maker looks into the lens, and the first words name it: 'You just closed on your house.' 1-3 s: the one thing only a fresh customer needs: 'Now listen' / 'there is really one thing you need' / 'you think it is only ...'.
do_words: 'After you buy your [thing], there is one ...'.
why: Only this week it is exactly about him.
