works_for: Services just begun or things just bought: braces, house, car, a police stop; seller known or not; warm-to-cold; goal save, watch, later choose; lasting paid ads in two winners.
care: What follows must help him that day, with nothing to buy first.

name: Let one measured fact of the product speak
method: Let one measured fact of the product speak
do_film: 0-1 s: the measured fact stands on the thing itself and fills the frame: the dial, the scale, the stamp, the pour; a finger points and leaves. Hold it still to 3 s while one plain sentence says what it proves for him ('this engine has 389,000 miles and still runs'). Nothing else in the picture. A fact that answers no wish of the buyer is not used.
do_words: Write the bland claim, ask 'because?', put the physical fact into the same line. Collect seven times more facts than you can use and take the one that surprises you.
why: One fact outweighs a hundred adjectives.
works_for: Me-too goods, price cuts, cars, soap, machines, old crafts, dog food; known and unknown sellers; goal believe and buy.
care: Measured and provable; it belongs to the product.

name: Say what he is, not his unknown name
method: Instead of an unknown person's name say his trade or the one trait that touches exactly what the product does or the thing that happens (the plumber before the drain, the one-legged golfer for balance); a role that changes nothing in this trade is left out.
do_film: 0-2 s: first line and title carry the role and the odd situation ('This Australian plumber was in for a surprise'); the person is at work in the frame. The name comes later, if at all.
do_words: Replace the name by the trade or trait: 'one-legged golfer', 'I'm a forensic artist'.
why: A role makes a picture; an unknown name makes none.
works_for: People your customers do not know by name; sport, trades, schools, golf; cold; goal stop.
care: The role is true.

name: The same job at very different price, time or size
method: The same job at very different price, time or size
do_film: 0 s: the whole row in one picture, smallest to largest, each with its number. Start at once with the cheapest or shortest. Each step rises; the biggest, already seen, comes last.
do_words: Title only the steps: '10 minutes, 1 hour and 24 hours', '$10 vs $1,000'.
why: He wants to know what more money or time really buys, and the last step is still owed to him.
works_for: Trades where the levels can be seen: photography, tools, gadgets, food; tiny accounts too; goal watch to the end.
care: All steps really made, the same maker and the same light.

name: Say what everybody believes, then test it at once
method: Say the claim, promise or belief that people doubt in the first sentence, and have its test visibly running by second three; show the result whichever way it goes.
do_film: 0 s: you hold the thing the claim is about, or stand in the test. First sentence (spoken or on the plate): the claim ('I was told this glue holds two trucks', 'Is fast food really fast?', 'This feature will save lives'). 2-3 s: the test is already under way; a second person doubts aloud if there is one.
do_words: 'You can't make a good X at home. Challenge accepted.'
why: He half believes it himself and wants to be told who is right.
works_for: Everyday services with a speed, price or strength promise; gadgets; food; cold; watching. Buyers' disbelief as first line when one kind of buyer is meant.
care: The result is shown whichever way it goes.

name: Two at one start line: a race with the numbers on
method: Two at one start line: a race with the numbers on
do_film: 0 s: two rivals on one line seen from behind or side by side at one table, each with its number or name; countdown already running. Go inside two seconds. Frame before the start on the cover.
do_words: 'X vs Y' with two superlatives; never tell the end ('tries to keep up').
why: The result is open and will be there in seconds.
works_for: Machines, tools, hand skills in a shop, delivery promises; watching.
care: A real race, both with a chance.

name: Start too close, then draw back to the truth
method: Start too close, then draw back to the truth
do_film: 0 s: so close that one misjudges (a calm face, one pair of glasses, a wall of steel, a house door). Within two seconds one smooth move back or one step of a person shows the real size or place.
do_words: 'At first it seems ... but then the camera zooms out.'
why: He has already made a guess and must see that it was wrong.
works_for: Anything whose size or setting is the surprise: trucks, fire bowls, glasses, models, property; cold.
care: The frame may mislead for a second, never about the product.

name: No words, only the sound of the work
method: When one hard or dirty job changes visibly under the tool: no speech, no music, no words on the film, only the sound of the work, first stroke within about two seconds, one job to the end.
do_film: 0 s: the dirty or unfinished thing fills the picture and the tool is at it or coming; you hear it. By 2 s the first stroke shows the difference (first clean stripe, first curl, first water). No music, no speech, no writing on the picture; one job from start to end, 10 to 60 seconds.
why: In a loud feed a clean sound makes the hand stop and the mouth water.
works_for: Trades, tools, cleaning, food with a sound; also dull business trades; watching.
care: Recorded on the spot, not from a sound library.

name: Give one proof of why to listen, before you teach anything
method: Promise what he gets and, in the same breath, show ONE checkable number from your own work (years, count, meter reading); never a bare name and title, never the firm's fame alone.
do_film: 0-1 s: the number itself fills the picture (finger on the meter, hand on the stack of finished job tickets) while the voice says what the viewer gets: 'I'll show you how to make your engine last.' 1-3 s: voice says the number once, the shot stays on it. 3 s: the first tip. No name, no greeting.
do_words: Promise and proof in the same line: what he gets + the years, the count or the profession that makes it true. The promise is never bigger than the proof.
why: A viewer asks first why he should listen to this person, and a number he can picture answers it before he leaves.
works_for: Teaching and service sellers (agency, lawyer, repair, courses); unknown or known teacher; cold, distrusting audience; goal: watch on, enquire. Not shown: everyday shop goods.
care: The number must be his own and checkable; a name and title without a proof is only an introduction.

name: How I did it, not how to do it
method: How I did it, not how to do it
do_film: Proof is headlines; film not shown in the library. 0-1 s: the low start and the finished proof in one picture, both in the hands of the one who did it. 1-3 s: "How I <exact thing>, after <low start>".
do_words: How I <result> / How a <odd small event> made me <result>, with the low start or odd cause.
why: One who did it is believed more than one who teaches it.
works_for: Courses, trades, makers, advisers with real work behind them; cold; goal: read, order.
care: It must be his own deed and number; no income promise.

name: Begin in the middle of the speaker's real day
method: Begin in the middle of the speaker's real day
do_film: Second 0: phone in the hand, the person is already under way: in the loaded car, walking to the job, at the airport door; the place can be read in the picture. No 'hi', no logo. Second 0-2: one sentence that says where he is going and what has just happened. Second 2-3: the thing or the one question of a customer stands in the picture.
do_words: First sentence says where you are and what you are doing: 'I'm on my way to ...'.
why: It does not signal an advertisement when it looks like the person's own post.
works_for: Toll badges, translators, lawyers, garages, car dealers, beauty; known and unknown speakers; cold; goals click and call.
care: Really that day and that place; the first second must already hold something to see.

name: Say the embarrassing thing in a lovely, made-up or elegant dress
method: Say the embarrassing thing in a lovely, made-up or elegant dress
do_film: Second 0: the loveliest opposite of the trouble fills the picture, plainly made up or elegant: a white-gloved butler with a silver dome, a puppet creature, a lady in evening dress. Second 1-3: in the same calm voice the plain truth is said; nothing disgusting is ever seen.
why: The picture makes it safe to look and to tell others.
works_for: Embarrassing everyday goods (toilet stool, spray, deodorant); unknown seller; cold; goals share and buy.
care: Two of the three films come from the same agency. Clean words; the holding's own films keep bodies covered and leave the coarse jokes out.

name: A line or a tune people can say back
method: A seller who will show many films opens every one of them with the same short, odd, sayable sentence or tune of his own that carries the name or the thing.
do_film: Second 0-2: the same odd sentence or short jingle with the name opens every film, over a plain piece of work. Make it copyable by a father at a paddling pool.
do_words: One short question or phrase, the same in every piece.
why: He knows how it goes and waits to say it.
works_for: Hamburgers, washing powder, toys, car dealers, plumber, pool cleaner; repeated use; goals be the one known.
care: Own words and own tune, no borrowed song without a licence.

name: Speak to the one who buys, not the one who uses
method: Speak to the one who buys, not the one who uses
do_film: Second 0: a person looks straight into the lens and greets the payer in two words ('Hello, ladies', 'For the aunts'), or the giver's moment stands there (a child's face lit by a tablet, the mother holding the books). Second 1-3: one order or one wish that only the payer has ('look at your man, now back to me', 'the gift of the year for boys'). The user is seen, never spoken to.
do_words: Headline addresses the giver or parent: 'gift of the year for boys'.
why: The one with the purse hears herself named for the first time.
works_for: Body wash, toys, children's and pet goods, gifts; goals buy.
care: The Old Spice actor is shirtless: take the address, dress the speaker.

name: The unknown thing said through a name everyone knows
method: The unknown thing said through a name everyone knows
do_film: Second 0: your strange thing in the hand, close. Second 0-1: voice and big letters say the likeness with the known name in it ('This is like an AirTag, turbocharged', 'It's like Uber Eats for the sun'). Second 2-3: the known thing is seen and shown to fall short, or yours does the one thing more (the hammer, the globe full of pins). Your own name is on the thing from second 0.
do_words: 'X for Y' or 'the Mozart of Gen Z' in title and first sentence.
why: What people know comforts them; what is wholly new makes them feel dumb and leave.
works_for: New, technical or dull things, unknown experts; seller unknown; cold; goals watch and buy.
care: The likeness must hold; no false link to the known brand.

name: Your thing beside the famous shop's, in the first frame
method: Your thing beside the famous shop's, in the first frame
do_film: Second 0: the famous thing with its name readable and yours at its side on one table or in two hands, both prices large if you are cheaper; or the famous one held out first, then a hard cut in the same pose to yours (by second 2.4). Second 0-3: one plain sentence that compares only what can be seen (thicker, 1 dollar, made at home). No face needed.
do_words: Famous name and your price in five words.
why: More people know the place than know you.
works_for: Food at home, drinks, perfume, boots, free meals; cheap everyday things; unknown seller; cold.
care: Fair comparison, no imitation sold as the original; her swapped backgrounds are not taken.

name: Begin with what he last did with you
method: Begin with what he last did with you
do_film: Sent to own customers only. Second 0: the maker or the receptionist at the bench, the customer's card or order in the hand. Second 0-2: 'You probably just placed your first order' / 'Your last cleaning was 23 months ago'. Second 3: what that means for his thing and the one next step.
do_words: 'Your X is now 3 years old and ...'; 'Previous gift: <date>'; a call: your name, his, and the free thing he took.
why: Only the one who really knows him could write it.
works_for: Watches, reference works, plans, donations, after a free download; own customers; goals come back, answer.
care: The date is right; no invented relation.

name: The odd means beside the trouble
method: The odd means beside the trouble
do_film: 0-1 s: the trouble close up (yellow tooth, gap, unplayed piano). 1-2 s: the unlikely thing comes in beside it (purple paste, yellow tape, a panel with numbers). 2-3 s: it touches the trouble. One fact why comes next.
do_words: 'Here's a strange way to ...' / the cure's odd parts listed ('3 sticks, a nail, and a bucket').
why: The distance between the trouble and the cure makes him ask how.
works_for: Visible results by unexpected means: whitening, dental work, learning music, fitness, rescue tools. Cold; goal stop, read, buy.
care: The means must really work that way and the speed must be true.

name: Open a closed thing slowly
method: Open a closed thing slowly
do_film: 0-1 s: the closed lid, box, sleeve, door or plain block fills the frame. 1-3 s: a careful hand works at it; it gives a little; a slit. The inside stays unseen until second 3 or later.
do_words: Name what it is closed on and for how long; the content comes in the next line.
why: He will not leave before he has seen what is inside.
works_for: Drains, fridges, tool cases, furniture, parcels, phone cases, secret soaps; resale and restoration; cold; goal stop and watch; sellers unknown to large.
care: What is inside must be worth it and must be shown.

name: Put him into the scene with a question he answers in his head
method: Stand him in one concrete scene and ask one question about himself that he can answer at once, yes, no or with one word; never a question whose answer only your text knows, and never a question that asks for the sale.
do_film: 0-1 s: the situation, seen from where he would stand (somebody behind you, somebody falls, the bus step too high). 1-3 s: 'Would you notice?' / 'What do you do?' Silence of one second for his answer.
do_words: A question with a picture in it instead of 'Tired of ...?': 'Does discomfort slow down your family adventures?'
why: He answers himself and is already the hero of the film.
works_for: Security, health, travel, parenting, first aid, socks; cold; goal watch, act; order value in one client test.
care: A true everyday situation, no fear beyond the fact.

name: Tell him the uncomfortable truth about himself, with a smile
method: Charge him with one true old habit or neglect, so exaggerated that he smiles, and offer the better way in the next breath; never with not having bought from you, never with his money, body or illness, and not from a seller he owes.
do_film: 0-1 s: one face straight to the lens, or the neglected thing in close-up; first words a short command or charge about the habit ('Listen up, the soap you shower with, you probably haven't even questioned it'). 1-3 s: the charge goes over the top, something silly moves in the picture. At 3-4 s the better way stands beside it. Nothing about 'you still haven't bought'.
do_words: 'Would you like to sit next to you at dinner?' / 'Your name has found its way into a little book on my desk.'
why: He feels caught, and the joke lets him stay.
works_for: Habits people have not changed, men's goods, magazines, overdue accounts; known and unknown sellers; goal answer and buy.
care: The charge is true and about a habit, never the body, the poor or the sick.

name: The strongest true word or number at the very start
method: To be seen: put the biggest true word or number into the first sentence (by its third or fourth word) and show in the same second the thing that proves it; no greeting, no 'in this film'. It does not by itself sell.
do_film: 0 s: the first word spoken and shown is the strongest one of the whole film (free, the sum, the record, the loss), with an act already running. Cut the modest lead-in. 2-3 s: the plain proof in the picture.
do_words: Move the last, boldest true sentence to the front; slide one carries only its sharpest words.
why: He decides by the first word whether this is worth a second one.
works_for: Business subjects, food shops, house tours, shorts and long films, carousels; known result and unknown face; cold; goal stop.
care: Every word holds: as wild as it can be while true.

name: A real customer, in her own place, tells what changed
method: For selling, not for reach: a real buyer's own phone film, unscripted, whose most surprising sentence about what changed is cut to the very front; then she shows the thing in use.
do_film: 0 s: her own phone film, face to camera in her kitchen, car or gym, already in the middle of the strongest sentence ('My husband tied my shoes. Since March I tie them.'), same words on screen. 2-3 s: she does it in front of the lens. No greeting, no product facts; other short voices only at the end.
do_words: Open with the then-and-now of one named person in one sentence.
why: She looks like him and has no reason to sell.
works_for: Everyday and dear goods, health, gyms, trades; unknown brand; cold; goal: buy, call.
care: A real buyer, her own words, result true and usual; consent in writing; no cure claims.

name: Two voices: one like him asks, the other answers
method: Two voices: one like him asks, the other answers
do_film: 0 s: the asker, face or voice like the buyer, already in the middle of the question. 1-2 s: snap to the one who knows, or the same person in another shirt. 3 s: first word of the answer.
do_words: "<Name>, is it really …?" as the first line, the answer as the second.
why: It is overheard, and the asker says what he would have asked.
works_for: Health, beauty, law, money matters, software, training; cold; goal: watch, enquire.
care: The asker must not be passed off as a real customer if he is not one.

name: Test a rumour in front of the camera
method: Test a rumour in front of the camera
do_film: 0-1 s: the thing at the lens, the size of it clear. 1-3 s: the claim that really goes round, with its number, "I've been told …" or "is it really as … as they say?", and behind it the test already standing (crane, stopwatch, scale); the first move of the test.
do_words: They say <claim with number>. We tried it.
why: The rumour sets the stake and nobody yet knows the answer.
works_for: Materials, food, gadgets, places, records; low budget; cold; goal: watch.
care: A rumour that really goes round; the test honest, the result shown.

name: Others like you already do it, you not yet
method: In a letter, message or reminder to one person who still has a due step to do (pay, file, book, sign): the true, high, local share who have already done it, and then "you are one of the few who have not yet".
do_film: Not shown in any film of the library. As a sent clip: 0-1 s: the row of doors (lockers, flats, shops) each with a tick; 1-3 s: the one without; text: "<true n> of <n> have done it. Yours is one of the <few> left." and the one step.
do_words: <n> percent of <people like you> have already … You are one of the few who have not.
why: Being the last of one's own kind is uncomfortable and easy to repair.
works_for: Duties, filing, habits, courses, event of the week; own list or a clear group; goal: act.
care: The share must be measured; 'effortless' claims must be true.

name: The true count of buyers beside the plain thing (stills and pages)
method: On a page head, still or title that meets people who do not know the seller yet: the exact true count of those who already bought, joined or watched, with the concrete thing; no stock photo, not as the opening of a film.
do_film: Not for film. Still: the thing alone on a plain ground, full width; under it the exact count and the stars with the number of reviews, nothing else. Page: the count in the first line.
do_words: Join 172,783+ <people like you> who … / <n> sold.
why: Many people like him have already decided.
works_for: Everyday goods, sign-ups, causes with many true buyers or reviews; goal: buy, join.
care: The number must be counted and current; a small true number beats a round one.

name: Show the very thing he owns or loves, first
method: Show the very thing he owns or loves, first
do_film: Second 0: one thing he owns, filling the frame and unmistakable (the red Model Y, the lens, the plane's blade, the husky), no logo of yours. Second 0-1: a hand or a tool comes to it and it moves. Second 1-3: its exact name is spoken and stands on the screen ('your Tesla Model Y', 'your hand plane'); your own thing enters only after.
do_words: First word and first picture are his thing by its exact name ('Tesla Model Y').
why: He sees himself before he is spoken to.
works_for: Accessories, hobby and trade goods, parenting; owners of a certain thing; cold; goal buy.
care: Film it at a real owner's.

name: Let the mishap open the film
method: Let the mishap open the film
do_film: 0-1 s: the calm work, close. First sentence already says it: 'Have we ever ... ? It just happened.' / 'My stick blender broke in the middle of a batch.' 1-3 s: the very moment or the damage itself, then the maker's face. Then how it was put right. Only a true mishap that harmed no customer.
do_words: 'Have we ever had a ... we couldn't ...? Well, we have now.'
why: Nobody shows his own mishap, so it must be true.
works_for: Makers, sweets, soap, dress cleaning, service and street films; small sellers; cold and warm; goal watch and trust.
care: A real mishap, harmless to the customer, and put right.

name: A voice tells one thing while hands do another
method: A voice tells one thing while hands do another
do_film: 0 s: hands already in a quiet, repetitive, visible job (nails pulled from a heel, gel filling a mould, curls swept into a jug). Voice begins in the same second with a person, a letter, an opinion. The job ends when the story ends.
why: The eyes are kept busy just enough for the ears to stay.
works_for: Craft shops, groomers, makers, personal stories; small unknown sellers; watching, then orders.
care: The story is true; customers agree to be told.

name: A bad word about your own product that turns out to be praise
method: A bad word about your own product that turns out to be praise
do_film: Second 0: the thing in full view, the complaint in big letters ('Why I'll never buy X again'). Second 1-3: straight face; the next line gives the reason, and the reason is praise.
do_words: 'Lemon.' / 'WARNING: these sheets make me call in sick.' The twist stands in the very next sentence.
why: All other advertisements praise; a complaint is the odd one out.
works_for: Pans, sheets, cars; everyday and dear; brand with humour; goals read and buy.
care: A real user or an obvious joke; never an invented review; the twist at once, so that nobody goes away with a false fault.

name: Many openings on one film; money decides
method: Many openings on one film; money decides
do_film: Film the body once. Film 2-5 different first scenes for it (with money 10-20), each on another idea; same small sum on each (Purple: $100 of views); look where the curve falls; keep the one that holds and sells; then change the ask.
do_words: Finish the body, print two headlines, same list, same day, roll out the better.
why: The opening is the cheapest part to change and changes the result most.
works_for: Paid video, mailings, crowdfunding; every sector shown.
care: One thing changed at a time, or you learn nothing.

name: Start from an opening that has already won
method: Take an opening that already won: your own best one, or one with which SMALL accounts or unknown sellers broke out in two or three places on the same trouble and the same kind of buyer; keep its idea and first seconds, make them better and truer for your thing, and repeat your own winner; never the form alone, never the one carried by a famous face.
do_film: Before filming: collect films on this trouble that strangers already watched far above the maker's usual; find the same idea in two or three places; keep its first seconds or its shape, join two proven themes, make it better and only then show your thing. When one of yours goes, make the next from it.
do_words: Same for headlines: keep the proved idea and its order, put your thing in.
why: What has stopped many will stop more; the risk is taken before the money is spent.
works_for: Every trade; shown for tongue cleaners, franchise advice, grocery-shop challenge, YouTube shows, herbal drinks; cold; goal all.
care: Rephrase and film anew; what is promised is our own product's.

name: Take the opening sentence from the buyers' mouths
method: Take the opening sentence from the buyers' mouths
do_film: Before filming: call ten buyers (10-15 minutes, no script) or read 500 reviews of things bought for the same trouble; note the sentence heard three times. Second 0: the picture of exactly that sentence ('I moved the bed' - the bed moves). Second 0-2: the sentence word for word, as a real buyer said it.
do_words: Use it word for word.
why: He recognises his own words.
works_for: Every client with at least some buyers.
care: Real sentences only.

name: Let the free showing choose what gets paid
method: Post short films that show the very thing you sell; put the offer and the money on the one that clearly beats your own usual number, and keep paying only while calls and sales come.
do_film: Post short films daily, or three cuts as trial reels to strangers; the one that clearly beats the others gets the offer and the money.
why: What stops people for free stops them when paid, and the maker guesses wrong.
works_for: Visible services, software, own channels; also accounts with a thousand followers.
care: Judge the paid run by calls and sales, not by views.

name: Draw the first picture before you write a word
method: Draw the first picture before you write a word
do_film: Sketch the first frame like a cover; would one click it? Draw several, choose or vote; only then words, as short as possible; then go and film it. The first five seconds are finished as carefully as a poster.
why: What would be clicked as a cover also stops a thumb.
works_for: Planned short and long films, series.
care: The film must deliver the drawn picture.

name: Judge an opening by sales, not by how many stop
method: Judge an opening by sales, not by how many stop
do_film: Use stop rate, hold rate and click rate only to find what is broken. Many stop, few buy: throw the angle away. Few stop, many buy: new first three seconds. Say in the first breath what you do and for whom.
why: A crowd that does not buy is a trailer.
works_for: Ad accounts, own channels, agencies, small shops.
care: For films whose goal is to be remembered, ask buyers how they heard of you (Bartlett).

name: Let them say it in their own words, no script
method: Let them say it in their own words, no script
do_film: Second 0: the real user or creator is already in the act (putting it on, opening it). Second 1-3: her own first sentence, kept with its small slips. Beforehand give four reasons to love it and how it is used, no script; she picks one. From buyers: a 10-15 minute unscripted call, keep the sentence.
do_words: Open with the buyer's or colleague's own sentence beside a real photo and first name.
why: His own reason sounds true, a read line does not.
works_for: Beauty, supplements, socks, cups, giving at work; larger creators and real customers; cold; goals buy and sign up. For an acted skit the opposite holds: cast people who can act (Cottrell).
care: Say nothing the person did not say; paid people are marked as paid.

name: Somebody they already follow for this very thing says it
method: Only a page or person whose followers already come for this very thing, who really uses it, in own words and from own page; not a small paid creator, not a celebrity of another subject.
do_film: Second 0: the face, hand or page his followers know, the thing already in use in her usual place (her car, her kitchen). Second 0-2: her own unscripted first words about it. Second 3: she shows the spot that convinced her. Posted from her page; paid work is marked as paid.
do_words: With permission put that name first, not yours; a short note from him says why.
why: The trust is already there and goes over with the sentence.
works_for: Socks, beauty, pool cleaning, pizza tools, masks, donations, software; unknown seller with a trusted go-between; cold.
care: Real use, permission, paid work marked as paid; no celebrity clip without consent; meta1-007 carries an alcohol brand on a shirt and tta3-004 a crop top - not to be shown as examples.

name: Write far more first lines than you need
method: Write far more first lines than you need
do_film: Before filming write 20-50 openings; as ten named makers would open it; past good taste for nobody's eyes; then walk the wildest back until it is true.
do_words: Plain how-to first as the measure, then 50-100 more.
why: Beyond what you know works lies the one that will really work.
works_for: Any first line.
care: The walked-back line must still be true.

name: The first picture works small, silent and alone
method: The first picture must be understood with the sound off and at phone size, with ONE thing large in the middle of its real place - not an empty ground - and the sound is made as well for those who hear.
do_film: Before it goes out play second 0-3 muted on a phone held upright: can a stranger say what is sold? One thing in the middle, brightest in the picture, in its real place; move cars, trees, passers-by out; hold it undisturbed for a full second. Then add voice or the thing's own sound.
why: The eye decides before the ear.
works_for: Feeds, covers, vertical films; about 80% never turn the sound on (Harmon).
care: Clean the real place; Hoyos's swapped backgrounds are not taken.

name: Go live from the workplace, the same hours every day
method: Go live from the workplace with hands at work in the picture; when an order comes in, pack it before the lens and say the name. Fixed daily hours help (Bannister, Newman), they are not proved as a must.
do_film: Phone fixed in a corner where the hands work, at chest height, so that table, product and hands stand in the picture. 0 s: hands already working. The owner greets and says what is being made now. When an order comes: take the piece, show it to the lens, say the buyer's first name (with consent), close the parcel. If a much-wanted article arrives, open its box live as the first live. Same hours as far as you can.
why: Like an open kitchen: nothing to hide, and his own order may be next.
works_for: Cheap gift food by post, street food, toy shop; warm followers and passers-by; visits and orders.
care: Clean workplace, customers' names only with consent, no auctions.

name: Repeat the winner with one big visible change
method: Repeat the winner with one big visible change
do_film: List your best. Same words, same shots - another person; then another place; or the same idea with a larger measure (3 games in 24 hours, seven in four days). The change must be seen in two seconds.
do_words: Same headline, another picture.
why: It shows whether person or message won, and proven ideas go on.
works_for: Any account with one clear winner.

name: Short words, short first sentences
method: In SPOKEN openings: the first three sentences four to eight words each and only words a child knows, at most one hard word in five seconds. In writing: simple words yes, short headlines no - the longer plain headline wins more often.
do_film: Say the first three sentences aloud: four to eight words each ('Biggest screen ever built. 20 times bigger than an IMAX.'). Strike every trade word and say what it means ('profit' becomes 'what is left'). At most one hard word before second 5. Read it to a seven-year-old.
do_words: Fifth grade or under on a readability check.
why: Each unknown word costs a second and the film does not wait.
works_for: Broad audiences, second-language viewers, tech, medicine, teaching.

name: Put most of the work into the first seconds, and give part of the promise at once
method: Put most of the work into the first seconds, and give part of the promise at once
do_film: Spend 20-30% of the editing time on the first minute, most on second 1. Second 0-2: deliver a piece of what the title promised. Then only the needed context, then no seam into the first action.
why: A bad start anchors the rest as bad.
works_for: Long and short films.
